title: fanoutqa: What are the largest moons of Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, and Jupiter? (a5f884779738c0c2)

chat_history.content: What are the largest moons of Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, and Jupiter?

content.content: We need to answer: largest moons of Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, and Jupiter. Mercury and Venus have no moons. Earth has one moon (the Moon). Mars has two small moons Phobos and Deimos; largest is Phobos. Jupiter has many moons; the largest is Ganymede. So answer list. Provide maybe sizes. Should be straightforward.

content:
**Largest natural satellites (moons) of the listed planets**

| Planet | Does it have moons? | Largest moon (if any) | Approx. diameter* |
|--------|---------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| Mercury | **No** | — | — |
| Venus   | **No** | — | — |
| Earth   | Yes | **Moon** (often called “the Moon”) | ~3,474 km |
| Mars    | Yes | **Phobos** (the larger of Mars’s two moons) | ~22 km (mean diameter) |
| Jupiter | Yes | **Ganymede** (the largest moon in the Solar System) | ~5,268 km |

\*Diameter values are approximate mean diameters; actual shapes are slightly irregular for the smaller moons.
